Alex / Rajiv / Natalie — attaching the redacted SOC 2 report and our pen test summary per Rajiv's ask (see attachments). Below are concise answers to Rajiv's two questions and a few extra items to help Procurement: 

1) Audit logs / retention:
- We provide streaming audit logs with token-level metadata including timestamp, route/model_id, request_id, user_id (if provided), and truncated token counts.
- Default retention (hosted): 90 days. For Dedicated/Private customers we support configurable retention via S3 export or push to customer SIEM for long-term retention.
- Export formats: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or CSV exports.

2) KMS / key management:
- Private deployments: customer-managed keys supported via AWS KMS and GCP KMS integrations; KMS-backed envelope encryption for model artifacts and KV cache supported.
- Hosted / Dedicated: we support provider-managed keys; customer-managed keys available for Dedicated with enterprise plan.

Procurement & SOW notes:
- I’ve included a one-page SOW template link in the MAP (HubSpot) and attached a standard SLA excerpt for latency p95 and availability.
- Standard procurement timeline we see: 2–4 weeks for PO and vendor setup after security sign-off, depending on legal review cadence.

Links / deliverables included here: HubSpot MAP (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/8901234), redacted SOC2_report_redacted.pdf, pen_test_summary.pdf.

If Rajiv wants the engineering team to join a call, Rishi can present the architecture and retention/export flow. Are you available for a short sync tomorrow 4/21 at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi all — quick follow from the engineering side with clarifications Rajiv asked for: 

- Audit log details: tokens are not stored as raw user tokens in exports; we store token metadata and hashed identifiers consistent with our data minimization policy. NDJSON schema attached as a short stub in this thread (example fields: timestamp, request_id, model_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, user_id_hash).
- Retention/export: For Private deployments we can configure daily exports to an S3 bucket you control; retention then follows your bucket lifecycle rules.
- KMS: Confirmed for Private: full support for AWS KMS customer-managed keys. We can provide an architecture diagram in the next sync.

Next steps: Rishi to join the 10am PT sync tomorrow to walk through architecture and answer Rajiv's technical Qs. Marissa — please let us know if Procurement needs any additional redlines in the SOW template before Natalie runs the checklist.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
